We know that we will fully switch to Presto in Dec, but we still use redshift for two important reasons: 


# Data reliability in Presto for our key ETLs - we are still in process of validating that ETL tables which were migrated to Presto are 100% accurate. e.g. we had a case where one of our ETL tables had duplicated orders, which made it completely useless. So before we make sure that it’s 100% reliable we still rely on redshift. But we are checking tables step by step and migrating as many queries as possible.
# Part of our notebooks/queries still run on redshift. denying new joiner access to Redshift would mean that he won’t be able to use some of the tools designed to help him run campaigns.

* Duration days value works

* Trait is added only in the city, where it’s configured
* Can activation trait have no earnings? = Yes

* Trait is added to courier created from Lead
* Fleet courier gets assigned the activation trait
* Trait is NOT added to manually created new courier (old partner)
** Trait earnings are not used for order with that courier
* Trait is added to manually created new partner + courier
* Trait earnings structure is used for order
* Trait is not added to courier which is created in status ‘Application’
** Trait is added after moving courier to status ‘Active’
* Activation trait earnings are taken into account on order proposal screen

Reverted back to recommending discount at a cohort level. We have reliable methodology to measure GMV uplifts at a cohort level (if the cohort itself is sizeable enough) since we are using Discount exploration campaigns to validate impact of model.

Used the following strategy to recommend discounts at user cohort level for different budget ranges

* Make user level GMV predictions
* Compute the mean of GMV predictions at a user cohort for all the discount choices
* Pick the discount choice which maximises the GMV predicted uplift/cost
* Use a threshold for the maximum predicted efficiency obtained above (whether or not to apply that discount to the cohort)
* Change the threshold, Compute the actual uplift to cost efficiency using the cohort level actual uplift values
* Plot the efficiency curve

Copying below external counsel’s feedback on Bolt Drive France to the question “*_Are there special requirements/regulations for the use of (dashboard) cameras? If yes, what are the main_*
*_requirements?” Although for BD_* dash cams normally face the street and are essentially used to investigate incidents it can be relevant in case the dashcams will record the road in front. 

external counsel feedback: 

“To be transparent, the legal regime applicable to the use of dashcam in vehicles is a grey area. To the best of
our knowledge, there is no specific regulation for dashcams in France. However, as a general rule, the use of
camera to film public streets is very restricted (as per the interior security Code). The French data protection
authority (CNIL) stated that “ Only public authorities (especially town halls) can film the public street. Neither
companies nor public institutions can film the public street. They can only film the immediate surroundings of
their buildings and installations (the exterior façade for example but not the street as such) in places likely to
be exposed to acts of terrorism. Private individuals can only film the interior of their property. They may not
film the public highway, including to ensure the safety of their vehicle parked in front of their home.”
This rules are designed for cameras installed on buildings or shops but by extension, same rules could apply
to cameras installed in vehicles as they would film the streets. In such case, an authorization from the
prefect is necessary.
At the same time, many insurance companies encourage the use of dashcams and the EDPB provided that :
“If a dash cam is installed (e. g. for the purpose of collecting evidence in case of an accident), it is important to
ensure that this camera is not constantly recording traffic, as well as persons who are near a road. Otherwise
the interest in having video recordings as evidence in the more theoretical case of a road accident cannot
justify this serious interference with data subject’s rights”.
In addition, such cameras trigger the questions of the application of all GDPR requirements: how to inform the
data subjects (persons passing nearby the car)? How to offer a right to oppose? Etc. We recommend to apply
as minimization techniques as possible (blurring of faces and licence plates, etc.) 


Generally, we are waiting for additional guidance from the CNIL on these issues. Alternatively, it could be
possible to directly contact the CNIL to obtain their position if Bolt is looking for a more definitive answer.”



Hope it helps

[~accountid:6075604653cc020069760c71] I have checked and this is related to the logic in Telema Integration which is looking up suppliers based on VAT, IBAN and Account Number. 

Here I see both the Suppliers have same VAT number and hence the issue. 

There is surely a need to revisit this logic as I see this being not 100% accurate to the current Business needs. 

So how integration works: 

Create Hashmaps - Hash maps is basically an indexed table (using the old SQL terminology) where we are storing VAT Number and Supplier ID. 

While processing invoices, we refer to this Hashmaps to get the first supplier which has the matching VAT ID. This logic initially must be based on the consideration that each supplier will have unique tax id. 

(In those cases) this would work perfectly fine however, in cases where there are multiple suppliers with same id, it would be random based on which supplier was read first when the hashmaps were created. 

I hope this helps.

useful query to find power users


{noformat}
select
	src.role_id,
	src.distribution_function,
	src.auth_type,
	src.reused_enrollments,
    src.first_name,
    src.last_name,
    src.email,
	count(1) num
from
	(
	select
		case
			tt.clone_options when '{"treatments_options":{}}' then 1
			else 0
		end reused_enrollments,
		tt.distribution_function,
		te.auth_type,
		alal.role_id,
        aau.*
	from
		public.targeting_test tt
	join public.targeting_event te
on
		tt.event_id = 
	join public.audit_log_audit_log alal
on
		alal.entity_id = 
		and alal.entity_type = 'targeting_test'
		and alal."action" = 'create'
    join admin_admin_user aau ON alal.role_id = aau.id
	where
		parent_test_id is not null
        ) src
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
order by
	1{noformat}

{noformat}      WITH global_multipliers AS (
      -- calculates global average multipliers per each number of days left in lifetime

        SELECT
          lifetime_1y_days_left,
          COUNT(*) AS cnt,
          -- GMV multiplier
          ROUND(AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur),1) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur_avg,
          
          COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur),1),0) AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_avg,
          ROUND((AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur)+AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur))/(1.0*AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur)),4) AS flv_gmv_eur_multiplier,
          
          -- revenue multiplier
          ROUND(AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur),1) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur_avg,
          COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur),1),0) AS lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur_avg,
          ROUND((AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur) + AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur))/(1.0*AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur)),4) AS flv_revenue_eur_multiplier
        
        FROM glue.ng_public.etl_rider_lifetime_ltv
        WHERE lifetime_1y_days_left IS NOT null
        and computed_on = (select max(computed_on) from glue.ng_public.etl_rider_lifetime_ltv)
        GROUP BY 1
      )
      
     select *

{noformat}--Churn % (“active” just means took a ride)------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--(Number of users inactive last 30 days but active within 30 days before) / (Number of users active between 60 and 30 days ago)
with all_active_users as (
	select distinct user_id
	from ng_public.etl_business_product_order_metrics
	where order_created_local_date between current_date - interval '60' day and current_date - interval '30' day
	),
num_recent_active_users as (
	select count(distinct user_id)
	from ng_public.etl_business_product_order_metrics
	inner join all_active_users using (user_id)
	where order_created_local_date between current_date - interval '30' day and current_date
	),
num_active_users as (select count(*) from all_active_users)
select 100 - ((select * from num_recent_active_users) * 100.00 / (select * from num_active_users)) as churn_percent
​
​
--Activation %--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--(Number of users inactive 60 to 30 days ago but active in last 30 days) / (Number of all inactive between 60 and 30 days ago)
with recent_active_users as (
	select distinct user_id
	from ng_public.etl_business_product_order_metrics
	where order_created_local_date between current_date - interval '30' day and current_date
	),
previous_active_users as (
	select distinct user_id
	from ng_public.etl_business_product_order_metrics
	where order_created_local_date between current_date - interval '60' day and current_date - interval '30' day
	),
activated as (
	select * from recent_active_users rau
	left join previous_active_users pau
	on rau.user_id = pau.user_id
	where pau.user_id is null
	)
select count(*) activated_percent from activated
​
--Conversion %--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--Share of users creating profile as % of those seeing sign up page
--PLACEHOLDER
​
​
--GMV increase %--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--(Sum of GMV in last 30 days) / (Sum of GMV between 60 to 30 days ago)
with gmv_l30d as (
	select sum(gmv_eur)
	from ng_public.etl_business_product_order_metrics
	where order_created_local_date between current_date - interval '30' day and current_date
	),
gmv_60_to_30d as (
	select sum(gmv_eur)
	from ng_public.etl_business_product_order_metrics
	where order_created_local_date between current_date - interval '60' day and current_date - interval '30' day
	)
select round(100 - ((select * from gmv_l30d) * 100.00 / (select * from gmv_60_to_30d)), 2) as gmv_increase_percent
​
​
--Rides increase %
--(Sum of Rides in last 30 days) / (Sum of Rides between 60 to 30 days ago)
with rides_l30d as (
	select sum(finished_orders)
	from ng_public.etl_business_product_order_metrics
	where order_created_local_date between current_date - interval '30' day and current_date
	),
rides_60_to_30d as (
	select sum(finished_orders)
	from ng_public.etl_business_product_order_metrics
	where order_created_local_date between current_date - interval '60' day and current_date - interval '30' day
	)
select round(100 - ((select * from rides_l30d) * 100.00 / (select * from rides_60_to_30d)), 2) as rides_increase_percent{noformat}

Simply put, we are working on creating different types of blocks to cover more specific situations - and more levels of accesses according to different criteria. Connections can be completely normal, as users have linked instruments. We have rules to prevent those users related to bad users from placing an order, there is no need to look at individual graphs from this point of view.

Hi [~accountid:61e918be38041c00686ad2bf] and @Clément, 

please find below some very first thoughts. More detailed guidelines for the business will follow. 

We understand that the automatic tool will search and extract specific information such as prices and RH service details in selected competitors’ apps for internal analysis purposes. From the background information we have, the tool won’t process any personal data.Therefore, data protection laws don't seem to be relevant at this stage. 

However, it would be relevant to consider the extracted data from other perspectives.

* Competitors (Uber and Heetch) prohibit data extraction from their apps and websites and this is clearly stated in their T&Cs (eg Article 10 (c)Uber General Terms of Use). Therefore competitors can sue Bolt for *contractual breach* and ask for damages.
* On top of that, given the potential frequency and high volumes of data processed and extracted, the tool may be able to recreate competitor’s databases. Database is protected by specific intellectual property rights. Hence, data scraping can be seen as an *infringement of database rights* and eventually this can also entail an infringement of trade secrets.

→ *Frequency* *and scale are key elements to be considered* *to assess the risk.*

In fact, the FR Cour de cassation mentioned those criteria in the recent decision regarding the web scraping case Le Bon Coin v. [Entreparticuliers.com|http://Entreparticuliers.com]

+*About the current practice:*+ the service is currently outsourced to a third-party service provider  (ie Majorel) selling us data that is manually processed and in lower volumes. Frequency is definitely lower and this reduces the risk. Under the current set up Bolt simply purchases data, the service provider bearing the risks in the event of third parties claiming an IP infringement. 

+*Next steps:*+ the topic is not new and past analyses have been run internally. Mariel is aware and asked to get more clarity on the legal framework and some guidelines. Julius is working alongside Mariel on this. Fayad Ktet is liaising with Data teams to understand what kind of data is needed locally and avoid excessive volumes of datasets and rather have better quality data. Once clarified the needs, Legal will produce deep dive research for FR + other countries - with the idea that Julius and Indrek will produce some Guidelines for the business. Expect 4-6 weeks until we get granular details for each market on what is legally allowed/ would constitute a bearable risk.

Therefore, from the legal standpoint it is rather unreasonable to launch the court proceedings for the recovery of the current debt.

Instead, we could do one of the following:

In any case, for the future, I would advise to rely on our General T&Cs with Couriers, which provide the following:

“_8.3._ […] *_No payments shall be made_* _if the amount payable to Couriers for the reference period falls below the minimum payment threshold established by Bolt or in case the Balance is negative after the reference period._ […]“.

This means that when the fleet/courier has a negative balance after one reference period (one week) we should stop all payouts to them and demand the repayment of the debt.

Also, under clause 9.1. of the General T&Cs:

“_9.1. So when we have evidence that the fleer/courier is in breach of our terms, we have the right to immediately suspend them from the platform or terminate the agreement.

Saving the query for *rider_predicted_ltv_aggregated*

{noformat}      WITH global_multipliers AS (
      -- calculates global average multipliers per each number of days left in lifetime

        SELECT
          lifetime_1y_days_left,
          COUNT(*) AS cnt,
          -- GMV multiplier
          ROUND(AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur),1) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur_avg,
          
          COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur),1),0) AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_avg,
          ROUND((AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur)+AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur))/(1.0*AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur)),4) AS flv_gmv_eur_multiplier,
          
          -- revenue multiplier
          ROUND(AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur),1) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur_avg,
          COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur),1),0) AS lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur_avg,
          ROUND((AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur) + AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur))/(1.0*AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur)),4) AS flv_revenue_eur_multiplier
        
        FROM glue.ng_public.etl_rider_lifetime_ltv
        WHERE lifetime_1y_days_left IS NOT null
        and computed_on = (select max(computed_on) from glue.ng_public.etl_rider_lifetime_ltv)
        GROUP BY 1
      ),
      
      etl_rider_lifetime_ltv_adjusted as (
      
      select 
      l.city_id,
      l.user_id,
      l.lifetime_1y_days_left,
      
      mm.gmv_model_accuracy,
      l.computed_on,
      l.lifetime_1y_start_date,
      l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur,
      l.lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur,
      
      COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur,0) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old,
      COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur * gm.flv_gmv_eur_multiplier, l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_new,
      
      
      COALESCE(COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur * gm.flv_gmv_eur_multiplier, l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur) - l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur, l.lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur)  AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new,
      COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur * gm.flv_revenue_eur_multiplier, l.lifetime_1y_ltv_revenue_eur) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_revenue_eur_new,
      COALESCE(COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur * gm.flv_revenue_eur_multiplier, l.lifetime_1y_ltv_revenue_eur) - l.lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur, l.lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur)  AS lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur_new
      
      FROM glue.ng_public.etl_rider_lifetime_ltv l 
      LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.rider_lifetime_flv_model_metrics mm ON mm.city_id = l.city_id
      AND mm.computed_on = (select max(computed_on) from glue.ng_public.rider_lifetime_flv_model_metrics)
      LEFT JOIN global_multipliers gm ON l.lifetime_1y_days_left = gm.lifetime_1y_days_left
        AND mm.gmv_model_accuracy = 'immeasurable'
      AND l.lifetime_1y_days_left IS NOT NULL
      LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city ON admin_system_city.id = l.city_id
      where l.computed_on = (select max(computed_on) from glue.ng_public.etl_rider_lifetime_ltv)
      )
      
      
   select
   user_id 
   ,DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) AS activation_date
      ,COUNT(distinct ltv_predictions.city_id) AS cities
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new) AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_revenue_eur
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur_new) AS lifetime_1y_flv_revenue_eur
   
   FROM etl_rider_lifetime_ltv_adjusted AS ltv_predictions
   LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.rider_lifetime_flv_model_metrics AS city_metrics 
   ON city_metrics.city_id = ltv_predictions.city_id AND city_metrics.computed_on = ltv_predictions.computed_on
   LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city AS city ON ltv_predictions.city_id = city.id
   LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_country AS country ON city.country_code = country.code
   LEFT JOIN (
      SELECT
      Distinct DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) AS activation_date_mapper,
      country.name AS country_mapper,
      MAX(Date(pc.month)) AS profitability_date_mapper
      FROM glue.ng_public.etl_rider_lifetime_ltv AS ltv_predictions
      LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city AS city ON ltv_predictions.city_id = city.id
      LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_country AS country ON city.country_code = country.code
      LEFT JOIN glue.ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rides_profit_rates AS pc
        ON pc.country = country.name AND DATE(ltv_predictions.lifetime_1y_start_date)>=date(pc.month) AND variable = 'Profit'
      GROUP BY 1,2
   ) AS dates_mapper ON dates_mapper.activation_date_mapper = DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) AND dates_mapper.country_mapper = country.name
   LEFT JOIN glue.ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rides_profit_rates AS pc ON dates_mapper.profitability_date_mapper = Date(pc.month) AND dates_mapper.country_mapper=pc.country
   
   group by 1,2{noformat}

We haven’t analysed the legal framework in FR or the CNIL standpoints on this question. However, this similar questions has come up before on other markets as well and I believe in general the approach is the same. 

The standpoint is that drivers would be considered as individual controllers under the GDPR when they would like to install and use such video cameras in the vehicles. They would determine the purpose (safety) and the means (video recording) for this processing activity. Bolt does not give any instructions on whether to install such cameras or require this in order to provide services on the platform. Also Bolt does not have access to the recordings or has any other means to control and ensure how/where such video recordings are stored, what are the access rules, security measures etc. 

Therefore, Bolt should be very cautious with giving instructions for this activity and moreover legal advice. We would not like to become the controller for this activity with the responsibility of ensuring compliance for such activity. 

However, I see that we could give limited guidance to drivers which clearly states that:

* Driver would be solely responsible for the compliance of installing and using any video cameras in the vehicles and recording the passengers. 
* Driver, as an independent controller, must ensure that they comply with GDPR and follow CNIL guidelines for such activity. Such obligations include, but are not limited to - ensuring that they have a legal basis for the activity, that passengers are notified about such recording, retention time is set for storing the recordings, appropriate security measures are implemented. 

On the discounts an encouraging the drivers to install dash cams → This should be done in a subtle way, that we let them know about the discount, but do not leave the impression of instructing to install such devices.

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_failed_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS failed_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_failed_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS failed_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT cast(substring(split_part(json_extract_scalar(r.input, '$.data.app_version'), '.', 1),2,2) as varchar) || ':' || cast(co.city_id as varchar) AS key,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment,
CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.user_rental_request r ON co.fraud_calculation_id = r.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND r.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'rental'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING 
	COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1
	AND (
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 1
	OR COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 0
	)
	AND (
	((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	OR ((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	)
ORDER BY
	fraud_payment_count_ratio DESC,
	failed_payment_count_ratio desc{code}

Hi [~accountid:625d48bdfd06270069bed4ec] 

please find below Privacy’s feedback on this matter: 

“We haven’t analysed the legal framework in FR or the CNIL standpoints on this question. However, this similar questions has come up before on other markets as well and I believe in general the approach is the same.

The standpoint is that *drivers* would be *considered as individual controllers* under the GDPR when they would like to install and use such video cameras in the vehicles. They would *determine the purpose* (safety) *and the means* (video recording) for this processing activity. Bolt does not give any instructions on whether to install such cameras or require this in order to provide services on the platform. Also Bolt does not have access to the recordings or has any other means to control and ensure how/where such video recordings are stored, what are the access rules, security measures etc.

*Therefore, Bolt should be very cautious with giving instructions for this activity and moreover legal advice. We would not like to become the controller for this activity with the responsibility of ensuring compliance for such activity.*

However, I see that we could give limited guidance to drivers which clearly states that:

* Driver would be solely responsible for the compliance of installing and using any video cameras in the vehicles and recording the passengers.
* Driver, as an independent controller, must ensure that they comply with GDPR and follow CNIL guidelines for such activity. Such obligations include, but are not limited to - ensuring that they have a legal basis for the activity, that passengers are notified about such recording, retention time is set for storing the recordings, appropriate security measures are implemented.

*On the discounts an encouraging the drivers to install dash cams → This should be done in a subtle way, that we let them know about the discount, but do not leave the impression of instructing to install such devices*.”

Some additional notes on the +use of dashcams to record public streets:+ 
using dash cams to film public streets is very restricted (as per the interior security Code). The French data protection authority (CNIL) stated that “ Only public authorities (especially town halls) can film the public street. Neither
companies nor public institutions can film the public street. They can only film the immediate surroundings of their buildings and installations (the exterior façade for example but not the street as such) in places likely to be exposed to acts of terrorism. Private individuals can only film the interior of their property. They may not record the public highway, including to ensure the safety of their vehicle parked in front of their home.” These rules are designed for cameras installed on buildings or shops but by extension, same rules could apply to cameras installed in vehicles as they would record the streets. In such case, +*an authorization from the prefect is necessary.*+

Let me know if you need further details. 

Thanks

Hi, 

although we are a simple platform that facilitates the transaction between drivers and riders,  and the transportation contract is concluded between rider and driver, in France Bolt platform qualifies as “*centrale de réservation*” under the FR Transportation Code.  As such the platform is responsible towards clients (i.e. riders) for the proper performance of the ride. This means that the platform is jointly liable towards riders, should the rider not comply with his obligations under the transportation contract. 

However, this applies to riders only and as far as I know *there’s no equivalent joint liability towards drivers.* 

Therefore, in the event of a lawsuit, we should have legal grounds to claim that the platform *cannot be held liable for losses and damages arising out from third parties breaches and misbehaviors, such as passengers allegedly assaulting the driver.* This is also outlined in Section 12.3 of Drivers T&Cs. 

+With respect to the initiative of proactively offering an indemnification++*:*+ I am of the view that only the court should determine responsibilities of the parties in the case at stake and allocate compensation for damages. Offering an indemnification might be misunderstood as a tentative of making the driver quiet and create a deterrent for the driver to take legal actions against the platform.  I would suggest to keep a more neutral position when it comes to offering an indemnification. 

+With respect to riders and the hard block+: we can rely on section 12.2 Riders T&Cs to suspend/terminate the provisions of the services to the concerned passengers. However, as far as I know we don’t verify the riders identity. Hence, riders could circumvent the account suspension and still create a new account with fake credentials.

Hope this helps

As discussed, here the flow summary and example Curl requests. Also, I did some more testing on the 3DS flow response (i.e. {{success}} = {{true}} and {{customer_action}} is not null) and in this case the {{card_id}} and {{customer token}} cannot be reutilised. Therefore there will be these additional actions to do:

* Delete customer token
* Create new customer token
* Create new card token

In summary, here is the flow for card verification:

# Create customer  _(to obtain cust_ID)_
# Create empty customer token _(to obtain tok_ID)_
# Tokenize a card _(to obtain card_ID)_
# Assign and verify customer token. From this you may have one of these four responses:

# A successful authorization ( {{Successful}} = *_true_* and {{customer action}} *_is null_* ) → Verification completed successfully
# An authentication-related soft decline if the issuer requests an authentication (i.e. {{success}} = {{false}} and {{error_type}} = {{card.needs-authentication}}) → Go through web flow and calling the {{makeCardToken()}} with the same parameters (cust_ID, tok_ID, card_ID)
# A 3DS flow response (i.e. {{success}} = {{true}} and {{customer_action}} is not null) → Delete customer token and go through web flow calling the {{makeCardToken()}} with *new tok_ID and new card_ID*.
# Another type of decline ({{success}} = {{false}} and {{error_type}} set to the error code) → you can follow your usual decline logic

Let me know if there is any other question or concern.

* _П.2.8.2 додано: «Сторони погоджуються з тим, що РІМ вважаються завіреними належним чином у випадку наявності на них кваліфікованих електронних підписів (КЕП) уповноваженого представника Комітента.»_

Це означає необхідність узгоджувати всі матеріали для розміщення через систему Вчасно. Ми не проти такого формату роботи. Але є вірогідність, що це сповільнить запуск кампанії. Будь ласка, опишіть, як буде виглядати процес?

*Можливість узгодження РІМ через Вчасно за цим пунктом є додатковою опцією, а не єдиною опцією, оскільки звичайний процес узгодження РІМ також прописаний у пункті 2.8.3. Для уникнення непорозумінь, додали слово “також“.*

* _П.4.8. У випадку порушення Комітентом терміну оплати рахунків за цим Договором, Агентство має право стягнути з Комітента пеню за кожний день прострочення в розмірі подвійної облікової ставки НБУ від простроченої суми за кожний день прострочення._ 

Повернули пункт. Будь ласка, аргументуйте видалення пені. Пеня має залишитися, незважаючи на тимчасове її нестягнення під час військового стану.  

*Повернули пункт, але змінили строк оплати рахунків у п. 3.4.*

* _П.4.9 У випадку порушення Комітентом терміну оплати рахунків протягом більше ніж 30 (тридцять) днів, Агентство має право розірвати даний Договір та стягнути з Комітента суму заборгованості та штраф у розмірі 10 % від розміру неоплаченої / несвоєчасно сплаченої суми. При цьому Комітент оплачує Агентству фактично виконані доручення / надані послуги та компенсує документально підтверджені збитки._

Так само просимо залишити це положення, але погоджуємося збільшити кількість днів прострочення, як умови застосування штрафу, до 30ти. Агентство залежить від своєчасчних платежів для успішного проведення кампаній.

*Повернули пункт із умовою про 30 календарних днів, але забрали положення про штраф, оскільки відповідно до п. 4.8. до простроченої суми вже застосовується пеня.*

* _П.7.3. Сторони дійшли до згоди, що дію даного Договору може бути достроково припинено в односторонньому порядку за ініціативою будь-якої зі Сторін з письмовим повідомленням про це іншої Сторони за 3 (три) календарні місяці до дати дострокового припинення дії даного Договору У цьому випадку Сторони мають провести повний взаєморозрахунок за зазначений термін. Припинення даного Договору в порядку, передбаченому п. 7.3. даного Договору, не вважатиметься односторонньою відмовою від виконання зобов’язань за даним Договором._ 

Просимо залишити в нашій редакції, 3 місяці, це наші корпоративні вимоги. Окрім цього, такі терміни зумовлені термінами відмови від доручень та завершення всіх документальних оформлень у зв‘язку з відмовами.

Using “Friends” without the proprietor’s consent could put Bolt at risk of trademark infringement if a UK trademark exists. It is highly likely that a trademark exists but we would need to carry out deeper research into the classifications that are protected to determine whether an advert using a protected trademark would put Bolt at risk of being asked to remove the advert or legal action being taken against Bolt. This could involve costly legal fees and potential damages, and lost management time when resources have to be diverted to defend the action. There is a good chance that Warner Bros, who are a large studio in USA, do have an appetite for pursuing infringers, as failure to act risks loss of their trademark, but we would need to gauge whether they have a pro-active trademark infringement “policy” and really how litigious they are. It is also worth reviewing the Committee of Advertising (CAP) Codes administered by the Advertising Standards Authority before going to advertising stage to ensure that any advert we release is compliant. 

I would recommend instructing external counsel to carry out a proper risk assessment before we do go to and advert and would be grateful for your thoughts before seeking a fee quote.

* Eater adds item(s) to their basket
* They proceed to checkout
* A 3DS prompt screen will appear in the Bolt Food app

* Simultaneously, they will receive a text message or email from their card-issuer/bank containing a PIN to insert into the Bolt Food app to confirm the transaction

* The user inserts the provided PIN in the Bolt Food app and clicks submit/confirm
* Their order is confirmed and the provider will start preparing it.

h1. New features proposal for Best Offer improvements

h1. +Time features:+

* is_weekend (0/1)
* weekday (0-6)
* hour (0-24)

h3. Continuous and Cyclical time features:

Time is treated as a continuous feature ranging from 0-1, where 0 is the start of time interval and 1 is the end. For example, in the case of “time_of_day” 00:00:00 is 0, 12:00:00 is 0.5 and 23:59:59 is 1. In the case of “time_of_week”, 0 is Monday 00:00:00 and 1 is Sunday 23:59:59. 

However, rather than calculating the values as floating points numbers, we calculate them as binned floating point values. For example, for “time_of_day”, the day is first divided into an arbitrary number of bins, e.g. “num_bins=24” where each bin corresponds to 60 minutes. The exact “time_of_day” is then mapped to the midpoint of its bin and then the floating point value is calculated. For example, time “14:20” is mapped to the midpoint of bin 14 (14.5) and then the floating point value is calculated as 14.5/24=0.6041. Note that the time “14:59” would have the same value, as it is in the same bin.

The “cos” and “sin” features aim to workaround the fact that 00:00:00 and 23:59:59 are only one second apart, however their values are maximally distant. The former has value 0 and the latter has value 1.  

For more details check: [https://github.com/sdaulton/TaxiPrediction/blob/master/2.%20DataPrepAWSSpark.ipynb|https://github.com/sdaulton/TaxiPrediction/blob/master/2.%20DataPrepAWSSpark.ipynb|smart-link]

* time_of_day_float_binned (e.g. 14:20 → 14.5/24 = 0.6041) 
* cos_time_of_day_float_binned (e.g. 14:20 → 14.5/24 → 0.6041 → cos(0.6041 * 2 * pi)
* sin_time_of_day_float_binned (e.g. 14:20 → 14.5/24 → 0.6041 → cos(0.6041 * 2 * pi)
* time_of_week_float_binned (e.g. Sunday 14:20. Sunday → 6, 14:20 → 14.5/24 → 0.6041, Sunday 14:20 → (6 + 0.6041) / 7 = 0.9434
* cos_time_of_week_float_binned (e.g. Sunday 14:20 → 0.9434 → cos(0.9434 * 2 * pi)
* sin_time_of_week_float_binned ( (e.g. Sunday 14:20 → 0.9434 → sin(0.9434 * 2 * pi)

h2. +Location features:+

* pickup_lat
* pickup_long
* pickup_distance_from_center (euclidean distance from center=[avg(pickup_lat), avg(pickup_lng)])
* destination_lat
* destination_long
* destination_distance_from_center  (euclidean distance from center=[avg(pickup_lat), avg(pickup_lng)])

h2. +User features:+

h3. Present features:

* age in years

h3. Historical features:

Features that need to be calculated on historical user data and require significant computation.

h4. *Definitions:*

*lower_price* = Discounted price if not NULL else price. Discounted prices are only sometimes available.

h4. Price features

* % cheapest rides last 365 days = (#rides with minimum lower_price / #rides)

Often low demand categories (e.g. “pet_friendly”) may have lowest price. These may not be applicable to the user or the user may never seen them, as they may not open the full categories view. Hence we consider alternatives to overcome this:

* % cheapest rides (economy or standard) last 365 days = (#rides (economy or standard) with minimum lower_price  / #rides (economy or standard)
* % cheapest rides (category position <=3) last 365 days = (#rides (category pos<=3) with minimum lower_price / #rides (category pos<=3) 

Averages are taken over median, as median is hard to calculate incrementally. Calculating a median over the past year is probably computationally infeasible. 

* Average ride price last 365 days = (sum ride prices / #rides)
* Average ride (economy) price last 365 days = (sum ride (economy) prices / # rides (economy))
* Average ride (standard) price last 365 days = (sum ride (standard) prices / # rides (standard))
* Difference Average ride price “Average ride (standard) price last 365 days“ and “Average ride (economy) price last 365 days”
* Average no order price (economy) last 365 days = (sum economy price given no order / # no order sessions)
* Difference “Average ride price last 365 days” and “Average no order price (economy) last 365 days”

h4. ETA features

* % fastest rides last 365 days (#rides with minimum ETA / #rides)
* % fastest rides (economy or standard) last 365 days (#rides (economy or standard) with minimum ETA / #rides (economy or standard)
* % fastest rides (category position <=3) last 365 days (#rides (category pos<=3) with minimum ETA / #rides (category pos <=3)
* % fastest rides given that standard_price <= economy_price * 1.10
* Max ETA accepted last 90 days

h4. Other:

* user conversion rate (#sessions with order / #sessions)
* user conversion rate given surge>1.0 (#sessions with surge>1.0 / #sessions)
* user conversion rate given no surge (#sessions with surge=1.0 / #sessions)
* Difference “user conversion rate given surge>1.0” and “user conversion rate given no surge”

home_city_id is available for each user, however the backend logic seems to change the home_city_id very rapidly. Therefore it is not perfect for classifying a user as a “tourist”. We calculate “home_country” and “home_city” by taking the country and city respectively with the most rides in the last 30 days.

* home country - country with the most rides in last 30 days
* home city - city with most rides in last 30 days
* is_city_tourist (home_city != city_id and home_country=country)
* is_country_tourist (home_country != country)
* is_tourist (home_city != city_id)

h2. +Context features:+

*Definitions:*

*CAT_X* = The category with most demand in a city. For example, CAT_2 would be the category with second highest demand in a city. In some cities, this is “standard” (Paris) in others it may be “autorickshaw“ (Lisbon). The time period for determining top categories corresponds to the time period of the training data, which is currently two weeks. 

Currently, the only price difference features are calculated based on price, which ignores discounted prices. Therefore we propose using lower_price.

* Difference lower_price standard and lower_price economy
* Difference lower_price CAT_1 and CAT_2
* Difference ETA CAT_1 and CAT_2

h2. Future consideration features:

* h3 cells instead of only lat/lng
* session based features such as #searches, has_rejection_in_current_session etc.

Hi there Inese!

You have the possibility to restrict/block these bad users by either placing a longer scheduled block or ticking the is_blocked button. In this situation, we would not take any *further* action in the Fraud team. 

As this is rather a social engineering then there is not much we can do. We can recommend you report the frequency of these (false) claims, and report and review the process internally in CS/HP for such situations. 

In general, social engineering fraud is fully reliant on the internal processes as the user does not act on it themselves - Bolt is the one who offers refunds and/or promos which they gain from. Meaning, the user itself is not really doing anything illegal as reporting an issue/asking for money back is not fraud per se. 

We would have the opportunity to not give them the satisfaction and that is why actioning based on relations is not the way to go here. This is a CS/HP process-specific problem regarding user behavior. 

Hope this explains the behinds of our standpoint a bit better. 

Cheers,

Hey!

Here is what I would do:

# The parties should have some agreement - we should avoid agreements with natural persons as this always poses some reclassification risk. 
# This should be an agreement of services. Meaning - we are setting KPIs what should be reached. How this is done - not up to us.
## It should be stated that _The Contractor is liable for having all the necessary licenses,  permits and self control plans for fulfilling the Agreement._ _The Contractor warrants that anyone acting on their behalf has received the necessary training and is prepared to fulfil the agreement adhering to the applicable regulations._
## The shipment term should be DAP, if not stated otherwise. The items must be transported in accordance with applicable legislation, including keeping items on a specific temperature, if applicable.
# Any employment agreement should be avoided as preferred solution. The general approach is that we don’t do part time agreements and the law restricts temporary agreements. Employment also means additional benefits, trainings and solving tons of health- and safety questions.
# The invoicing should be based not on the fixed fee, but rather KPIs.
## Official communications should be agreed (how is delivery schedule made - how much should be notice period, how is order deemed accepted).
# The agreement could include some additional provision should we want to use transport services in addition to the agreed scope. This can be done via fixed fee/time fee/distance fee.
# As this would be like any other agreement, the invoices should be sent to a designated email address. Prepayment should be avoided and payment term could be 10 business days after submitting the invoice.

Regarding Ops employee:

# It is legally allowed to have several employment agreements. The person could be employed by Bolt Store EE OÜ, but:
## We don’t do part-time agreements;
## Any employment agreement is connected to a benefit package;
## We would be responsible for health and safety training;
## We have to pay social tax contributions and we have some threshold for that;
## We have to calculate leave pay.

This means, employment would be considerably more expensive. If we compare base fees - to a company we shall pay 1200 EUR (net of VAT) per month. Employment would cost us 1954 EUR. Extra 754 EUR - PIT, social tax contributions etc.

Pursuant to Article 9 of the employment agreement concluded between the employee and her current employer (the Employment Agreement), the employee is subjected to several restrictions, and limitations.

In the present case, Articles 9.2(i) and 9.3(v) of the Employment Agreements are applicable. According to Article 9.2(i) of the Employment Agreement during his employment with the company, the employee shall not, whether directly or indirectly engage in any other business or have an outside commercial interest except where the employee has obtained the company’s prior written consent in relation thereto. Article 9.3(v) states that unless otherwise decided by the company upon termination, for a period of 12 months after the termination of his employment with the company and without the prior written authorization, the employee shall not, whether directly or indirectly engage in any business competing with the company or any company belonging to the same group of companies.

The Clause is mentioned twice in the Labor Code of Georgia (the Labor Code), particularly: (1) when the parties are in the employment agreement; (2) when the employment agreement is terminated.

As per Article 16.5 of the Labor Code, an employee's right to be employed for more than one full-time or part-time job may be restricted by an employment agreement if the person who is to be substituted is the employer’s competitor. Article 60.1 of the Labor Code also states that an employment agreement may provide for an employee's obligation not to use the knowledge and skills acquired in the course of fulfilling the conditions of the employment agreement in favor of an employer competing with his/her employer. The situation after the termination of the employment agreement is stipulated in the second sentence of Article 60.1 which sets forth that the limitation can be envisaged up to 6 months after terminating labor relations, on condition that during the period of said limitation the employer shall pay the employee remuneration of at least the amount that the employee was paid at the moment when labor relations were terminated.

In the given case, Article 9.3 (v) of the Employment Agreement includes 12-month restriction period, therefore the Clause is enforceable partially, provided that there is respective remuneration also agreed for that limitation, that we have not seen in the provided excerpt of the employment agreement. Which means that after expiration of 6 months, as indicated in Article 60.1. of the Labor Code, employee is no longer obliged to comply with 12 months restriction period.

2.      Violation of the Clause

As per the information provided to us, the Client is considering hiring a candidate who currently works at a competing company. She works as a marketing manager in Georgia and is responsible for one market, Georgia. The Client intends to hire her as a global marketing manager. She would be in charge of courier acquisition and would relocate to Tallinn, Estonia.

The question is whether the Clause is limited by territory or by the scope of the rights and obligations of the employee. Numerous legislations provide that the Clause shall be restricted with, inter alia, components of duration, geography, scope, and competitors. Moreover, there are jurisdictions in which such contracts have been examined by the courts that have deemed non-compete to be legally binding so long as the clause contains reasonable limitations as to the geographical area and period in which an employee of a company may not compete.

However, according to the practice of Labor Inspection in Georgia, because the Clause protects the employer from employees' precarious actions, such as disclosing confidential information, using skills and knowledge gained while employeed, etc., the Clause inter alia is not limited by territory or by the nature of the work. In case of violation of the obligations stipulated in the Clause, only the relationship between the two companies is evaluated and taken into consideration. In particular, whether these companies represent each other's competing companies regardless of the geographical area.

It is our understanding that companies in the present case, namely Wolt and the Client can be considered competing companies and if the potential employee takes the job the Client offered, it shall be deemed as a violation of the Clause by the employee and not you.

You shall also be mindful that if the penalty for breaching the Clause is not expressly stated in the contract, in such circumstances, it is difficult, if not impossible, for the employer to demonstrate to the court what damage was caused to him and how much compensation should be paid by the employee.

1.2.4              Potential Risks for the Client

The person liable for breaching the Clause is an employee, not you. If the present employer commences civil actions, submits a request, or conducts any action, it will be addressed toward the employee.

For formal purposes, you are not required to check the employee's current employment agreement, so you will not have any information regarding the Clause, but for interpretation purposes, you as a competing entity must have a reasonable expectation that the employee is restricted by the Clause. That is solely for demonstrating your good faith. you cannot be held responsible for breaching a clause that you did not agree to, however, there is important issue to be considered, in particular:

According to the Artcile 9.4 of the Employment Agreement, in the event that during the Employee’s employment or during the restrictive period set out above, the Employee receives an offer of employment that is not from a group company or the Employee is requested to provide services to a person, company or entity that is not a group company, the Employee must inform such person, company or other entity making such an offer or request that the Employee is bound by the terms of this Agreement.

Hence, the Employee has an obligation to inform the Client on agreed restrictions in question. By doing so, the Client becomes or should have become aware of the restriction which might imply non-contractual obligations for the Client, which is highly unlikely to be proven, but still, in terms of understanding of good faith principle, it might give the Employer possibility to bring allegations that the Client was aware or could not have been unaware of the fact that such breach of the Employment Agreement by the Employee might have led to damages, that will be subject to further burden of proof of the Employer.

To conclude, for avoidance of any doubts and unexpected misunderstandings, it would be reasonable for the Client if the Employee obtains written informed consent from the Employer on termination of the Employment Agreement and entering into agreement with the client.{quote}

'Soft Opt-in' means that marketing communication is permitted if:

* there is/was existing relationship with recipient;
* the entity sending the marketing is the same legal entity that collected the recipient's details initially;
* the marketing relates to "similar" products and/or services provided by the entity which initially obtained the recipient's details; and
* the recipient is given the opportunity to opt-out every time. 

So cold calls and e-mails cannot be based on this. Basically LT regulation rules out such cold direct marketing altogether. But my advice is to reach out to those leads and ask them for consent for further communication. Of course this may not be 100 % in line with the regulatory expectations, but it is an approach to take if conducting such activity.

In short, the preference from legal would be to have essentially a delivery agreement and preferably with a legal entity, rather than a natural person (as this poses reclassification risks). 

# This should be an agreement for delivery services. Meaning - we are setting the KPIs that should be reached. 
## It should be stated that _The Contractor is liable for having all the necessary licenses, permits, certifications and self control plans for fulfilling the Agreement (i.e. compliance with food safety etc)._ _The Contractor warrants that anyone acting on their behalf has received the necessary training and is prepared to fulfil the agreement adhering to the applicable regulations._
## The goods should be delivered to the designated places unloaded. The items must be transported in accordance with applicable legislation, including keeping items at a specific temperature, if applicable.
# Any employment agreement should be avoided as a preferred solution. The general approach at Bolt is that we don’t do part time agreements and the law restricts temporary agreements. Employment also means additional benefits, trainings and solving tons of health- and safety questions.
# The invoicing should be based not on the fixed fee, but rather KPIs.
## Official communications should be agreed (how is delivery schedule made - how much should be the notice period, how is order deemed accepted etc).
# The agreement could include some additional provision should we want to use delivery services in addition to the agreed scope. This can be done via fixed fee/time fee/distance fee.
# As this would be like any other agreement, the invoices should be sent to a designated email address. Prepayment should be avoided and payment term could be 10-14 business days after submitting the invoice.

Regarding Ops employee:

# It is legally allowed to have several employment agreements. The person could be employed by Bolt Store EE OÜ, *however*:
## As mentioned above, we don’t do part-time agreements;
## Any employment agreement is connected to a benefit package;
## We would be responsible for health and safety training;
## We have to pay social tax contributions and we have some threshold for that;
## We have to calculate leave pay.

This means, employment would be considerably more expensive. If we compare base fees - to a company we shall pay 1200 EUR (net of VAT) per month. Employment would cost us 1954 EUR. Extra 754 EUR - PIT, social tax contributions etc.

If we do opt to enter into a service agreement but with a natural person rather than a legal entity - then we will need to involve tax team as well for some further considerations. 

Best, 

Liisa

Hi [~accountid:5e65e969c54d0a0d04427b8c] 

From a legal perspective, if a driver has duplicate accounts, this could mean that they are in two different places at the same time and it would be reasonable to suspect the driver of fraudulent activity. Under our terms and conditions, we can immediately suspend a driver’s access to the Bolt Platform and to the Bolt Driver Account for the period of investigation, if we suspect an infringement of the Agreement or fraudulent activity from the driver’s behalf and I would recommend suspending accounts in such circumstances.

The next consideration is whether suspending or kicking a driver off our platform would hinder us from a regulatory perspective. On the issue of duplicate accounts in general, I have been discussing this ticket with Larry, who confirms that from a regulatory perspective, if we have data about a driver from another country, we *may* want to use it to see if there’s any adverse information from that non-UK account which would stop us from letting them on our platform. However, in reality, we take the council’s stamp of approval on the driver when they are licensed so if the driver is licensed with the council, the assumption is that they are fit and proper to do so unless otherwise (i.e. from passenger complaints). We have no idea how stringent or effective other country’s processes are to rely on and it is not part of our considerations if the driver is licensed in another country.  And so, really duplicate accounts may be useful for data collected using the platform but not necessarily for licensing purposes.

I hope this information is helpful and will close this ticket.

If you have any queries relating to duplicate accounts in future, feel free to raise a new ticket.

Best wishes

Shiv

Hi [~accountid:61000f7aec92ab00706384aa] , [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] 

as this ticket is privacy-heavy, please see input from data protection perspective below, as there are couple of issues to consider with such data acquisition:

1. General comments

As the provider is a separate data controller, it should ensure that it has the legal basis to process and disclose the data. Generally speaking, where possible, we are suggesting to include this in a contract, however the potential liability would be on the provider, even if there is no contract in place.

2. Marketing consent

Given that planned contact would be marketing in nature, standard requirements for marketing communication should apply: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3712188879/Marketing+Communication+Privacy+Requirements|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3712188879/Marketing+Communication+Privacy+Requirements|smart-link]. As in this scenario soft opt-in cannot be relied upon because Bolt has no previous relationship with the prospect driver, the consent would be appropriate way to legitimise the contact.

It would be helpful to understand if the leads provider can ensure that it has obtained consent from the leads for receiving direct marketing messages. If so, Bolt could rely on this consent, otherwise reaching out to the leads may be classified as unsolicited marketing. [~accountid:61000f7aec92ab00706384aa] - is this something lead provider could ensure?

The other approach-  that may come with some risk- would be for Bolt to reach out to the acquired leads and ask them for marketing consent within first contact. Of course this may be not 100% aligned with regulatory expectations, but may be another solution to consider in line with team’s risk appetite.

3. Notification requirements

For newly acquired databases, Bolt needs to deliver on the notification requirements, i.e. present the leads with Bolt privacy policy ([https://bolt.eu/fr/legal/fr/privacy-for-drivers/|https://bolt.eu/fr/legal/fr/privacy-for-drivers/|smart-link]) within one month after the data is obtained, at the latest at the time of the first communication to that data subject.

4. Data subject rights

If any of the leads acquired would reach out to Bolt and ask for their data to be deleted, Bolt would be required to comply with such request.

I have carried out a review of the Maintenance Contract for a fire alarm (Equipment), Preventative Maintenance and Monitoring as below. I am assuming that we only want already have a fire alarm and do not require installation of new Equipment but do correct me if I am mistaken.  

Some initial questions:

* If we already have an alarm in place, what is the £150.00 charge for Equipment on the ANNUAL MAINTENANCE CONTRACT document? 

Key terms within this agreement are: 

*Notice* - 2 months written notice to Innovation is required for Bolt to terminate the maintenance services which is agreeable to a short term arrangement like this. 

*Obligations* - if the alarm goes off to the Alarm Receiving Centre, you will need to notify Innovation. If we change the layout of the office, you will need to notify Innovation. It is Bolt’s responsibility, not Innovation’s, to ensure that the phone lines are working properly and that the account is properly maintained to ensure that signals such as video data or alarm activations are sent across to Innovations Alarm Receiving Centre. If we don’t fulfil this obligation and a security incident occurs, Innovation won’t be liable for this. Telephone line, rental and call charges are Bolt’s responsibility too. 

*Liability* - Innovation excludes liability for any work, repairs or replacement of Equipment which results from fire, electrical power surge, storm, flood, accident, neglect, misuse or malicious damage which is acceptable given these trigger events are outside of their control. However, we need to be careful that the Equipment is not being misused to avoid being held liable in such circumstances.  

Innovation excludes liability for any loss or damage if the alarm is neutralised, circumvented or otherwise rendered ineffective by unauthorised persons which concerns me because our primary reason for requiring maintenance of our alarm system is to ensure security and that it is not tampered with. Innovation does have insurance cover in place to mitigate risk for claims made against it in respect of accident, injury, loss or damage and failure to perform and wrongful advice unwittingly, but I would not recommend signing this agreement without seeing the insurance cover they have in place and which, in accordance with this agreement, we can request a copy of their insurance certificate. 

Bolt’s liability is uncapped which is also concerning as we are not the party providing the service and in the first instance, I would not recommend agreeing to this. It would be in our best interests to negotiate a cap on liability to the value of invoices paid under the agreement. We may have general insurance cover in place to mitigate the risks here but we should go back to Innovation on their insurance and a liability cap for Bolt in the first instance.  

*Additional charges* – there are additional charges under this agreement for call out as detailed on the ANNUAL MAINTENANCE CONTRACT document for “reactive maintenance” but it is not clear whether this falls within Corrective Maintenance. Before signing, I would obtain clarity on what reactive maintenance is. There are also charges at 2% interest above base rate for late payment and, although this is a standard term, I would recommend diarising the monthly payments and ensuring that they are made on time as we have been penalised for late payment in the past and want to avoid this.

Before signing this agreement, we need clarity on quite a few points, including the extent of the service provided, the insurance cover Innovation has in place and whether Innovation will accept out liability cap. I would be grateful if you could get back to us on the questions above. Depending on this, the next step would be to go back to Innovation for clarity on the Specification, their insurance cover and request that they cap Bolt’s liability. 

Best wishes

Fraud team has three use cases for identity verification:

# *When we determine that identity needs to be verified during ride hailing check order*
## In this case, we have city_id from the order, thus can be implemented without problems
# *When user retries verification flow*
## If user experiences a technical difficulty (connection issue, technical error, etc.), user can press “try again” button in which case, user sends request to fraud-user service to get a Veriff session (either existing pending or a new one)
## In this case, we do not have city_id explicitly since the request is coming from the mobile device
# *An experiment to collect user Device ID via Veriff*
## Idea was to validate if Veriff device ID is better than in-house device ID
### More details: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3431893046/Veriff+Browser+ID+Testing|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3431893046/Veriff+Browser+ID+Testing|smart-link]
## Solution was to execute headless Veriff flow on client side without any UI/UX to get the device ID
### For this, a public endpoint was exposed for mobile clients to use to trigger the verification flow via Fraud server and towards Identity team
### Done as part of [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/FRAUD-2323|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/FRAUD-2323|smart-link]
### Result: Veriff ID was not good enough and the experiment ended
#### More details: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3712221199/Veriff+device+id+VS+Bolt+device+id|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3712221199/Veriff+device+id+VS+Bolt+device+id|smart-link]
## Since the hackish experiment has been concluded, we should remove any remaining code from client and server side

Hi [~accountid:6242def45f63fd0069b130bd] and [~accountid:624407b42e101c006a8d8cf6] 

you have two options when it comes to ask users a refund for any damage they caused to the Bolt Drive vehicles: 

# *Contractual penalties*

A contractual penalty is a provision by which one party commits to pay something to the other in case of breach of contract. The amount is determined in advance and reflects an estimate of the potential damage that a party may suffer. 

In the framework of FR Bolt Drive T&Cs parties agree to several contractual penalties applying to the defaulting user. Under these conditions, Bolt can charge a penalty upon prior written notice without going to court. In such a case there’s no need to provide any evidence of the actual damage. 

If the indemnification is too low compared to actual damage, then Bolt can ask the judge to adjust the penalty. An invoice of actual repair costs incurred will be required then. 

*2. Seeking damage compensation in court*

If no contractual penalty has been agreed upon by the parties, then Bolt may seek indemnification in court by providing the invoice of the actual repair costs incurred on top of other pieces of evidence. 

+*Nota*+: 1 and 2 are alternative options. The existence of a contractual penalty limits the possibility to ask for damages in court. When a contractual penalty applies, Bolt cannot claim for damages in addition to the penalty.

Happy to discuss it in deptht tomorrow during our meeting.

As it turned out we also need to support {{+40372}} variant as it’s also a mobile phone in Romania

* Currently for legacy, there is no pre-auth request coming from Balance → Payment for {{amount = 0}} so all the following payments are failing with {{Token Missing}} error.
* The intended functionality with modern Apple Pay flow is to always perform pre-authorization regardless of amount. So payment is expecting an {{Authorize}} request from Balance -> Payment regardless of amount. 
* Currently the decision is happening on Balance layer when to call for {{Authorize}} (for 0 or any other amount). At this point Balance won't know if the request will be processed via legacy or modern Apple Pay flow. 
* In legacy world, we don’t exactly know how the functionality will behave when we start sending pre-auth with {{amount = 0}}, it needs some testing from payments and balance side before we rollout this functionality for legacy. For modern Apple Pay we know that nothing will break. 

I suggest to start rolling out this feature for legacy for targeted users first to analyse the behaviour before we target wider user base.

I have been testing out Web Worker API through Partytown to take GTM scripts off the main thread. Here are a couple of findings and notes from my side:

*Advantages*

* It will move GTM and scripts that are loaded by GTM off the main thread and we will receive much better ratings on Google performance reports. The score will be very similar to the one without GTM integration and will be at least 80.

*Disadvantages*

* We need to set up a reverse proxy in CF ([https://nystudio107.com/blog/creating-a-reverse-proxy-for-partytown-with-aws-cloudfront|https://nystudio107.com/blog/creating-a-reverse-proxy-for-partytown-with-aws-cloudfront|smart-link]). It is required because third-party scripts [require a proxy to work in Partytown|https://partytown.builder.io/proxying-requests]. You may visit [this link |https://www.gatsbyjs.com/docs/reference/built-in-components/gatsby-script/#proxy-configuration]for more details regarding the proxy configuration. In our case, we will need to configure the proxy for third-party scripts that are included via GTM, Cookiebot, Google Optimize, FB Pixel, etc. And the configuration needs to be updated every time we want to add new scripts via GTM.
* Partytown is still in beta, so if we even set up the proxy properly it is not guaranteed that GTM and other third-party scripts will work properly.

A task was created to address the required functionality as a result of the research: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/WEB-2978|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/WEB-2978|smart-link]

Provided this is a one-time thing (at least until we have completed the wider assessment) we can give the green light to these daily campaigns (e.g. do X deliveries on Saturday, get Y). 

Hourly campaigns (e.g. do X deliveries between 6pm - 9pm, get Y) are still a no-go I’m afraid. The risk here is that we are putting more pressure on couriers to work during a defined window, so it’s more difficult to defend this as a pure incentive rather than a control mechanism. 

As a side note we should also try to ensure that these kind of campaigns are achievable - if we are requiring an unrealistically high number of deliveries per day, this also has the effect of pressurising couriers to work during the full time of the campaign rather than still being able to accept/reject orders freely and still stand a chance of achieving the incentive.

Hi all, 

From e-money regulation perspective, the key questions are:

* 1st, is the issuer of Bolt Drive Credits is an entity other than the local entity offering Drive as rental service, if yes, those credits can be considered e-money;
* 2nd, if they are different, the key item through which it would at all be able to challenge the e-money qualification is whether exchanging the car against Bolt Drive Credits is considered issuing those credits “on receipt of funds” within the meaning of EMD art 2(2).

So, practical questions you first need to consider are:

* who is legally the entity issuing such Bolt Drive Credits to the individual (is it the same entity who offers services, i.e. French local entity);
* how can you actually use such credits (e.g. if those would be used via Bolt Balance, then Bolt Balance issuer is Bolt Operations OÜ; practically we can’t currently restrict the use of Bolt Balance to drive only etc).

Thereafter it’s possible to address any more detailed questions.

{noformat}WITH unnested_table AS (
SELECT
SPLIT(a.user_id,'lead-driver-',2)[2] AS hashs
,a.traffic_source.name
,a.traffic_source.source
,a.traffic_source.medium
,cast(JSON_EXTRACT(CAST(event_params AS json), '$.page_location') as array(varchar))[1] as page_location
FROM
  bigquery.ga4_analytics as a 
WHERE
  event_name = 'Driver Signed Up'
  AND event_date >= date_parse('2022-02-01','%Y-%m-%d') AND event_date < date_parse('2022-10-01','%Y-%m-%d')
),

acquired_drivers AS (
SELECT 
  COALESCE(fleet_driver_registration_log.hash, unnested_table.hashs) AS lead_hash,
  fleet_driver_registration_log.id AS lead_driver_id,
  fleet_driver_registration_log.driver_id,
  unnested_table.name,
  unnested_table.source,
  unnested_table.medium
FROM
  ng_public.fleet_driver_registration_log as fleet_driver_registration_log
INNER JOIN
  unnested_table AS unnested_table
ON fleet_driver_registration_log.hash = unnested_table.hashs
WHERE
  unnested_table.name LIKE '%Search, Drivers, Nigeria, Conversions%' -- Replace with campaign name
  OR unnested_table.page_location LIKE '%google_search_driver_ng%' -- Replace with UTM
)

SELECT
  count(distinct drivers.driver_id) as total_activated_drivers,
  count(distinct drivers.lead_driver_id) as total_activated_leads
FROM

INNER JOIN 
  acquired_drivers as drivers
ON
  orders.driver_id = drivers.driver_id
WHERE
  ride_price > 0

_Rest assured it is always the intention of Bolt to disclose personal data to the police wherever it is permitted to do so. Bolt takes its law enforcement cooperation responsibilities seriously and the company regularly makes disclosures to law enforcement agencies in response to such requests._

While Data Protection Act 2018 provides some exemptions from the application of UK GDPR, the disclosure needs to be connected to the investigated issue._

_The nature of the request- as it has been indicated in the submitted Request for disclosure of data under the Data Protection Act 2018- is a speculative inquiry and hence widely exploratory, the threshold of criminality is unknown, and the link mentioned between requested data points with criminal activity to Bolt operations is vague and based on assumptions about what certain data points could indicate. The potential, even inadvertent, loss of those third party's right to privacy must be warranted in these circumstances, and the use or intention of that data upon disclosure explained (at least at a high level)._

_Bolt therefore cannot test for necessity and proportionality nor undertake and document an assessment for lawful disclosure - as required by law. In short, compliance with the current disclosure request conflicts with other legal obligations with which Bolt is required to comply i.e. data protection._

_Any previous request of similar nature will be reviewed and any rectification to our internal procedure will be done if deemed necessary to comply with applicable data protection legislation._

Does the RGPD affect the rules on prospecting?
No: The RGPD does not change the rules applicable to canvassing emails, whether they are B2B or B2C. More information on the CNIL website: [https://www.cnil.fr/fr/la-prospection-commerciale-par-courrier-electronique|https://www.cnil.fr/fr/la-prospection-commerciale-par-courrier-electronique|smart-link] 

On the SNCD website:
[https://www.sncd.org/consentement-pour-les-emails-btob-en-france/|https://www.sncd.org/consentement-pour-les-emails-btob-en-france/|smart-link] 
As long as the message is related to the profession of the person being canvassed, you do not need an OPT-IN (or prior consent).
So the RGPD has nothing to do with it and nothing changes as it stands.
On the other hand :

* you must offer a valid OPT-OUT on the BtoB email.
* you must of course respect all the provisions of the RGPD, in particular: right to information, unsubscribe, data security…

* Moving forward, we deal with the grievance first before moving to consider any formal performance assessment and dismissal. We need to ensure it is fairly assessed, if his performance has improved we need to accommodate date this.

Hey!

You are right - the aim of the legislation is to give some transparency to the consumers regarding the discount. I have had several discussions how the mechanism should be implemented, but the general idea is that we have to show the lowest price during the 30-day period*.

*_Here is the thing - there are two different approaches to this. There are retailers who think the discount has to be lowest price during the 30-day period and there are retailers (like Rimi) who display the lowest price during the 30-day period next to the current discounted price._ 

I did some reading and reached a conclusion that we have to show the lowest price during a 30-day period (_surprised Picatchu_) - this means, if we have a price increase, we have to use the price before the increase as the point-of-reference. _For example: Can of Pineapple slices was sold for 5 EUR, but the price increased to 6 EUR, and we want to have a promotion for it, then 5 EUR shall be the point-of-reference. If we decide to sell it for 4 EUR, the discount is 20%, not 33%._

And as far as I can understand, there are no limits on the campaign periods/cooling off. We could have several promotions, we have to keep in mind the rules (if we have continuous price reduction, we have one set of rules, if we have 2 independent campaigns during 30-day period, another set of rules).

I found a guide written by Estonian CPA. Even though it’s not Latvia, the core principles are the same:


* _If an earlier price is published, it must be ensured that the earlier price published in the price reduction notice was also the lowest price applied by the trader to the commodity during the previous 30 days, even if the lowest price was valid for only one day. This means that, when notifying the price reduction and calculating the preferential price must be based on the previous price, i.e. the discount percentage to be applied must be calculated on the basis of the lowest price of the last 30 days._  
* _The link between the previous price and the discounted price is important to ensure that the consumer understands the price advantage offered at the particular point of sale and is not misled by the granting of a price advantage._ 
* _Therefore, the earlier price must be the price actually applied by the trader at that outlet and not merely a marketing tool to make the discount more attractive. If necessary, the trader must be able to prove to the enforcement authority (by means of logs in the information system, database extracts, screen captures, etc.) that an earlier and reduced price has been applied, and to describe the principles of price indication and discount calculation._ 
* _The price reduction notice must indicate the correct previous price, i.e. the lowest price of the goods for at least the last 30 days. No other prices need to be quoted for comparison. For example, you do not have to indicate in the notice what the normal selling price of the goods is or what the goods were selling for yesterday. If you wish to indicate other prices, you must first indicate the lowest price in the last 30 days in addition to the promotional price._
* _If the price of a good has been unchanged for the last 30 days, there is no need to change the price label for that good and the previous price is the price currently on the price label. However, if the price of the goods has been increased in the meantime, or other discounts have been applied, then the price label must be adjusted to show the correct reference price, i.e. the lowest price in the last 30 days._
* _If the price of a good is gradually reduced without interruption, it is not always necessary to start from the lowest price of the last 30 days. In the case of an uninterrupted gradual reduction, the price before the first reduction may be indicated as the earlier price. For this purpose, the lowest price in the 30 days preceding the first price cut notice must be taken into account and may remain the earlier price for all price cut notices in the same campaign._
* _This only applies if the price is reduced gradually without interruption and the continuous reduction does not increase the previous published price._ +_In the case of a series of promotional campaigns over a period of 30 days, with interruptions between each campaign and price increases, the promotional campaigns are considered to be successive promotional campaigns._+ _In this case, for each successive discount, the previous price will be the lowest price during the last 30 days and not the previous price before the first promotional campaign._


I hope this helps you a bit. If not, please let me know and I’ll get back to you asap.

a) mis on täpne kuupäev ja kellaajaline vahemik, millal toimunud sõitudele vasteid otsitakse;

* GAs estimate adjustment factors that they apply to their forecasts.
