_IKÜM artikkel 6 lg 1 sätestab andmete töötlemise võimalikud õiguslikud alused. IKÜM art 6 (1) (c) ja KrMS § 215 lõike 1 alusel on andmete küsimiseks tõepoolest olemas õiguslik alus. Siiski tuleb igasuguse andmetöötluse puhul järgida ka eesmärgipärasuse ja minimaalsuse põhimõtet. Kuna päringuga küsitakse väga laia andmekoosseisu, siis sellisele päringule saaksime tulemuseks tuhanded vasted. Suure tõenäosusega ei ole kõik sellised vasted kriminaalasja lahendamise seisukohalt asjassepuutuvad. Hetkel on taotluse olemus veel väga lai, kuritegevuse künnis on teadmata ning soovitud andmepunktide ja Bolti teenusekasutajate kuritegeliku tegevuse vaheline seos on ebamäärane. _Nõustume, et andmete väljastamiseks eksisteerib seadusest tulenev õiguslik alus ning soovime väljastada kriminaalasja lahendamiseks vajalikud andmed. Kuid selleks, et päringu skoopi piiritleda, paluksime täpsustada järgmiseid asjaolusid:_ 
_a) mis on täpne kuupäev ja kellaajaline vahemik, millal toimunud sõitudele vasteid otsitakse;_

_b) mis on uuritava kuriteo eeldatava toimumiskoht ja selle seos Bolti teenuse kasutajatega;_

_c) mis on konkreetsed andmed, mida vastena saadud kasutaja kohta soovite._

_Antud päringule vastamine küsitud ulatuses ja ilma täiendava võimaluseta veenduda andmete väljastamise proportsionaalsuses on vastuolus vastutava töötleja kohustustega, mis tulenevad isikuandmete kaitse üldmääruseses sätestatud isikuandmete töötlemise põhimõtetest._

*Goal:* The goal of the experimentation is to improve the utilization of scooters that are fully/close to fully charged in the charging docks.  

*Usecaae*: 70% of our users use the scan button to scan a scooter before a ride, Users in this usecase would be prone to take the scooters that they see closest to them in the charging docks. 

*Assumption*: Based on a loose assumption that if we nudge the users to a scooter that has a higher charge, there could be an uplift of conversation of scooters that are charged but under-utilised. 

*Experiment:* With a controlled group setup, we are aiming at a 20-30% conversion of the feature 

*What we know:* Users check the battery level before they take a scooter, but if the battery percentage is good but not low, they take the scooter anyway. It would be hard to convert users iin such scenarios as they would have already decided to take the scooter.

Hi [~accountid:61addb80b0b630006a695081] and [~accountid:5c050dbbd9499e1a8fbcc92c] 

As discussed, I wanted to ensure we had a pension sacrifice form compliant for the UK market. Please see attached the template recommended from our UK employment specialist with relevant guidance issued from them for future reference. *In short, we can provide this template to employees who would like to utilise this option and it does not need to be an addendum to their employment contract.* 

* In order to effect a salary sacrifice in the UK, there must be a variation to the contract of employment (if the sum being ‘sacrificed’ is a contractual entitlement), usually by way of an ‘opt-in’ form. In order for the variation to be effective there must be a clear understanding between the parties as to the terms of the arrangement and in particular the employee must fully understand the implications of what they are entering into. 
* However, based on my understanding here, the business wishes to permit the sacrifice of a range of ‘non-salary’ payments which are made to employees fairly regularly (e.g. overtime payments, night-time fees, on-call bonuses, sales bonuses) on an ongoing basis – not just an annual bonus.
* Please note, it is an essential feature of salary sacrifice that remuneration is given up before it has been ‘received’. In relation to annual bonuses, we often see companies writing to employees to inform them of the value of any bonus and when it will be payable, and then offering them the opportunity to sacrifice it (or a portion of it) to the pension find, provided they do so before the bonus is due to be paid.  
* Attached is the draft template which can be used or adapted for these purposes. You do not need to issue this alongside contracts. *You can make it available on Bolt’s intranet (confluence) and sign-post employees to it in an email (slack), or bulletin.* In order to ensure that employees fully understand the implications of what they are entering into, it is best practice to issue separate guidance to them. If you have an existing FAQ sheet related to salary sacrifice, that could be shared with employees alongside the form.

* This request is the first time a request clearly references both fleets and partner, and a criminal case
* *Until confirmed, we should assume that both the partner and referenced fleets are subjects to the criminal case investigation*

* _Accordingly the instruction to not share the request should be carefully considered and the consequences weighed_

* HU Tax advisors have at first look advised that this request does not necessarily create additional risks for Bolt
* However, the likelihood of the identified risks in [tax memo and tax calc] materialising is probably increasing

* *PROPOSAL*

* Draft reply without further involvement of Partner, [@peter.westin|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U02J3J47542] will manage and coordinate information.

* Engage outside criminal lawyers to ascertain and advise on Bolts position.

Had a discussion with [~accountid:6172754ef485cd006863a3a8] and [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] 

To summarise the questions:

# We have the terms and conditions for the use of Bolt brand. We don’t have any contractual penalties for enforcing them. This means - if we want to have the branding removed, this will be a longer process as we don’t have the implementation mechanism for that. This means, we have to contact the person/next in line to have the logo removed. If they do not comply, then we should apply for a court. This is long (and expensive) process.
# We should have some uniform approach to this question. Should we include contractual penalties? If yes, how can we implement them. Should we make someone an example? If yes, how will this impact our supply. This is something we cannot answer as this is mostly political/business decision. Both approaches have their strengths and weaknesses. If we decide to implement contractual penalties, this would mean changing the applicable TnC-s and we would have to assess the possible risks (abuse of dominant position has been assessed, the reclassification risk has not been assessed).  
# We don’t have quick means for restricting the use of our logos/brands if a person does not have legal grounds for using them. This means, we should go through the official notifications and civil procedure. Only thing that could sway the user are the costs of civil procedure and damages. Then again - if the person doesn't officially have any assets, the threat of monetary loss is not really something that they deem to be essential. As we have our budget limitations for the proceedings, this should be informed decision - most likely outcome is us having high expenses with diminishing returns. 
# Regarding the drivers currently active on our platform - our branding terms and conditions have objective criteria for demanding the branding to be removed. Is this TikTok video only situation we have had? I think if we can demand the removal of the branding, we have other grounds to deal with the driver (as stated in section 4.3. of the driver TnC-s). Do you have real-life examples of such situations where we should require the branding to be removed?

Hi [~accountid:61027984a539cb006846c64f] - I am not sure I understand your question or what it is that your are intending to do? I think the main point here is transparency to the consumers regarding any discounts - the general idea is that we have to show the lowest price during a 30-day period. As long as we are compliant with that, I am not sure I understand the relevance of how many days there are in between promotional campaigns?

How does the price can change “before” or “after” a promotion - would that not be a start/continuation of a promotion or a start of a successive promotional campaign? 

If we are talking about progressive reduction - then the reference price is the price before starting the reduction. 

We cannot artificially inflate a price to then show a “bigger discount” as this would be misleading. If we have a price increase, we have to use the price before the increase as the point-of-reference. _For example: can of pineapple slices was sold for 5 EUR, but the price increased to 6 EUR, and we want to have a promotion for it, then 5 EUR shall be the point-of-reference. If we decide to sell it for 4 EUR, the discount is 20%, not 33%._

Here is some guidance from the EE Consumer Protection Agency, the general principles should apply in LV:

* _If an earlier price is published, it must be ensured that the earlier price published in the price reduction notice was also the lowest price applied by the trader to the commodity during the previous 30 days, even if the lowest price was valid for only one day. This means that, when notifying the price reduction and calculating the preferential price must be based on the previous price, i.e. the discount percentage to be applied must be calculated on the basis of the lowest price for the last 30 days._  
* _The link between the previous price and the discounted price is important to ensure that the consumer understands the price advantage offered at the particular point of sale and is not misled by the granting of a price advantage._ 
* _Therefore, the earlier price must be the price actually applied by the trader at that outlet and not merely a marketing tool to make the discount more attractive. If necessary, the trader must be able to prove to the enforcement authority (by means of logs in the information system, database extracts, screen captures, etc.) that an earlier and reduced price has been applied, and to describe the principles of price indication and discount calculation._ 
* _The price reduction notice must indicate the correct previous price, i.e. the lowest price of the goods for at least the last 30 days. No other prices need to be quoted for comparison. For example, you do not have to indicate in the notice what the normal selling price of the goods is or what the goods were selling for yesterday. If you wish to indicate other prices, you must first indicate the lowest price in the last 30 days in addition to the promotional price._
* _If the price of a good has been unchanged for the last 30 days, there is no need to change the price label for that good and the previous price is the price currently on the price label. However, if the price of the goods has been increased in the meantime, or other discounts have been applied, then the price label must be adjusted to show the correct reference price, i.e. the lowest price in the last 30 days._
* _If the price of a good is gradually reduced without interruption, it is not always necessary to start from the lowest price of the last 30 days. In the case of an uninterrupted gradual reduction, the price before the first reduction may be indicated as the earlier price. For this purpose, the lowest price in the 30 days preceding the first price cut notice must be taken into account and may remain the earlier price for all price cut notices in the same campaign._
* _This only applies if the price is reduced gradually without interruption and the continuous reduction does not increase the previous published price._ +_In the case of a series of promotional campaigns over a period of 30 days, with interruptions between each campaign and price increases, the promotional campaigns are considered to be successive promotional campaigns._+ _In this case, for each successive discount, the previous price will be the lowest price during the last 30 days and not the previous price before the first promotional campaign._

Please let me know if anything remains unclear. 

Best, 

Liisa

Hi [~accountid:61979e9c744c4d006971e9df] - there is no definition of what is *“perishable or soon to expire goods”* under the LV regulation or what are goods *“liable to deteriorate or expire rapidly”*  in the EU directive. 

Guidance on the interpretation states that goods which are ‘liable to deteriorate or expire rapidly’ are perishable goods that may need to be discounted more often in order to sell them faster due to approaching expiration dates. 

This notion is also used in a Consumer Rights Directive, but it does not define the ‘goods which are liable to deteriorate or expire rapidly’. The compliance with the objective criteria of being ‘liable to deteriorate or expire rapidly’ is to be assessed on a case-by-case basis. *Examples of goods liable to deteriorate or expire rapidly are fresh food and drinks with short expiry time limits*. This possibility for Member States to derogate from the general rule on price reductions cannot be applied to goods that are not perishable because of their physical composition and properties but only ‘expire’ in the commercial sense, such as seasonal clothing.

I think we have to apply some common sense here that reference is made to fresh food/drinks - unless such items do not expiry rapidly and have a long shelf life. A long shelf life is the only way in which we can meaningfully be considering perishable food in the context of a +30 day rule+ regarding price reduction. 

[~accountid:60d07638a1746300707e7c74] my first question is, are restaurants selling goods that are *not* perishable, using the above context? Are there partners on the food app that sell -alcohol-, clothing or household goods or foods with a long shelf life - I think it helps to be precise as possible here. Because to me, in an ordinary context, a restaurant provides fresh food/drink - but it may well be more nuanced than that so I cannot give you a blanket response here without understanding this better. 

I think that the document that you are referring to is not making a distinction between perishable/soon to expire goods and talking about the price reduction rules in more general terms. 

Perhaps [~accountid:5f3f8efd91e67a003fc4551a] if you could also outline what is the concern from your end and what examples do you have of this rule being applied to products that it should not (food with short shelf life?) then this would also help us understand what the practical issues are and what needs fixing. 

Thanks all,

Hello, [~accountid:5d43ea3f1a6bf10be6db0f6e], 

Thank you for looking into our request and for your fast response! 

Our main goal for changing this particular page (we do not necessary need to do so for all KB pages) is *to provide more clarity for our drivers and fleet owners about these new features*.
Reason: They tend to see them as a negative initiative from our side: We cut their freedom of using the platform as they wish / need to. (Eg: Some FO state that we 'enslave' the drivers through such metrics). 

While the overall information is very informative, the way the message, more specifically the phrasing of the article is very hard to be understood in a positive way. 
Why: The translation is too formal. 

What we did in the suggested document, was to keep the idea of each paragraph (we did not alter the information), and phrased in a more informal, friendly language.
You can take as an example the 1st paragraph: 
RO: _Scorul șoferului și rata de acceptare sunt valori folosite pentru a evidenția interacțiunile potențial dăunătoare sau periculoase dintre șoferii parteneri Bolt și pasageri. Scopul lor este de a vă ajuta să îmbunătățiți calitatea serviciilor pe care le furnizați._ 
ENG: _Driver Score and Acceptance Rate are metrics used to highlight potentially harmful or dangerous interactions with Bolt platform. Their purpose is to help you improve the quality of service you provide._
Changed into: 
RO: _Există două modalități prin care este evaluată calitatea serviciilor oferite de către tine pe platforma Bolt: rata de acceptare și scorul șoferului. Cele două reprezintă noi modalități prin care interacțiunea potențial dăunătoare sau periculoasă dintre un șofer partener Bolt și pasager vor fi evitate. Acest lucru ne va ajuta să oferim un mediu mai sigur pasagerilor, dar și șoferilor parteneri Bolt pe platformă._ 
ENG: _There are two ways in which the quality of the service you provide on the Bolt platform are measured: Driver Score and Acceptance Rate. The two new metrics are used to avoid as much as possible the potentially harmful or dangerous interactions between a Bolt driver partner and a passenger. This initiative will help the platform to be safer for the passengers and the Bolt driver partners too._ 

*Other relevant observations that you can take into account from our side:* 
- The pronoun we use to address the drivers in the Romanian translation is either formal, either informal. I checked with the local marketing team and we should go with the informal one. Again, to be more friendly and supportive for the Bolt driver partners; 
- Some examples given in the article - as the one that [~accountid:5d95f00336d2520dde7ede18] mentioned: *o**_rders with some location and/or timing features_* - are not understood by us, as the local ops team, least of all will the drivers or fleet owners understand them. That being said and to also answer your question, it is not poorly translated, but its reference / meaning is irrelevant and does not point exactly to which type of order it refers at. This kind of language frustrates the drivers and make them even more suspicious about our intentions (I know that sounds silly, but it’s true);
- While I can understand that we do not have our _Internal Complaint-Handling System Rules for Business Users of Bolt_ page translated in Romanian, the drivers or fleet owners won’t. Why? Not all of them speak English; 
- Visuals. I’m trying my best to get the reasoning behind not having visuals, but in the same time I consider we should make exceptions for some features. Why? We leave in a media / video oriented era where everybody plays videos to make dinner. It’s not that the feature is not intuitive, but it’s a new feature and we should give the driver a handy help to understand it at first. On the same note, just speaking my mind here, I don’t get why we do not have training-like videos for some of the features that might be considered sensitive by the drivers. Again, I’m asking for your help here to think it through and see if we can find, together, a solution. As for this argument: 'drivers have limited time between the trips, so the articles should be easy to navigate through'. If that is true, that means they also cannot read / follow a 1000 words article while driving. 

Let us know your thoughts! Also, do you know how the process of posting / editing new KB pages works? Do local teams (ops / CS / marketing) proof read them and so on? 

Many thanks, 
Alexandra

From ~ 12:17 October 13 till ~15:00 October 18, Veriff didn't expire and abandoned any sessions. As a result, when the issue was fixed on the Veriff side on October 18 we got a spike in sessions' timeouts. 

Regarding why we didn’t timeout all related verification on our own when they reached 7 days old.  Each time when {{FlowRunFinalizerCron}} picks up a row it tries to finalize the row and if not the cron sets {{next_execution_lower_bound_ts}} to {{now() + Math.pow(2, counter + 1)}}: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/8812246ad6d229b79b08667dded23351668c2616/src/platform/identity_verification/identity_verification_process/main/table/FlowRunFinalizationAttemptTable.ts#L116|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/8812246ad6d229b79b08667dded23351668c2616/src/platform/identity_verification/identity_verification_process/main/table/FlowRunFinalizationAttemptTable.ts#L116].  

It means that the retries will happen in {{1, 2, ... 2^(attempt_count)}} seconds + time between cron execution, event emitting and handling. It means that attempt 18 will happen after {{(1 + ... + 2^18 sec = 2^19 - 1 sec ~ 6.06814814815 days}} and attempt 19 after {{2^19 - 1 sec ~ 12.1362847222 days}}. Since our current timeout for verifications is 7 days and 5 minutes and the time between cron execution, event emitting and handling takes less than a few minutes, for most of the “hanging” verifications, we will finalize them only after 12 days. 

It is quite an unexpected behaviour, so it might make sense to amend the retry logic in a way, so the {{next_execution_lower_bound_ts}} will be always less or equal {{row.created +  this.config.fail_flow_run_after_sec}}.

We didn’t encounter this issue before because usually, Veriff works fine: it expires sessions after 7 days and sends a webhook to us.

Stuff that was figured out while trying to release this:

* Builder Agent has {{bepl}} namespace hardcoded. For deployments we can get from the deployment template. For purge/health we can get it from CDS by describing the service.
* Builder Agent swallows any errors from k8s API for create deployment. Then health check runs and since the service was already deployed and healthy, deployment will succeed even though it actually failed to deploy the new version. This means that k8s services versions will lag behind and the developers will miss it.
* We need to namespace names of resources when accessing them from a different cluster. E.g. instead of {{etcdgateway:2379}} we need to do {{etcdgateway.bepl:2397}} 
* Service namespace is determined like this: 
** At release time, Builder reads the services' Bootstrap path
** Code owners (GH users/teams) are determined by matching the Bootstrap path to the CODEOWNERS file from bolt-server develop HEAD
** Using static mapping file in bolt-server develop HEAD, from code owners we get the Vertical
** From Vertical we get the namespace using a simple transformation (most of the time is Vertical lowercased, minus the {{ENG-}} prefix)
* Because of this, a service’s namespace can change without engagement from BEPL or SRE. This will happen if CODEOWNERS or static mapping file is updated. In this situation, the updated service will get deployed to a different namespace, resulting in 2 parallel deployments. We can either implement something to prevent this, or have a detection mechanism that will engage SRE to terminate the old deployment.

Hello [~accountid:620b9b75878c2f00729892b6] ,

The Time off in lieu absence plan is a global absence plan and so the behaviour is the same for others countries which are using it.

*Why does this error pops up and prevent workers to request time off in lieu :*

As of today, there is no accrual calculation on this absence plan, that means that, by default, none hours is entitled on this absence plan. Moreover a rule has been defined on this absence plan in order to prevent worker’s time off in lieu balance to go below 0. 

So, as 0 hours are accrued by default and as a lower limit balance is set up to 0, each time a worker try to request time off in lieu, Workday prevent the request as it would trigger the balance below the lower limit defined.

*How to allow worker to request Time off in lieu :*

First step is to manually edit the time off in lieu accrual amount for the concerned worker. Then worker would be able to request time off in lieu within the absence calendar page.

N.B: please find enclosed some screenshot.

*Regarding the case we have discussed by DM :*

A worker is working on bank holiday (agreement with manager), and this worker would like to “exchange” this bank holiday day with a working day in order to be off.

You or us (under discussion) will need to run the task “Maintain Accrual and Time Off Adjustments/Overrides” on worker’s profile => action => Time and Leave. On this task select “GBL - Time Off in Lieu Accrual” then “8” (as we assume one full day is equal to 8 hours) then on period column indicate the month on which the bank holiday worked occurs, then I highly recommand to add a comment for follow up purpose.

Regards

Measuring HP impact

* HP unavailable for most of the DEX datasets I used (so no reliable way to simulate HP impact)
* Regular weekly campaigns don’t have HP enabled usually (because of the opportunity cost of not targeting) but in special cases (eg: while testing different targeting methodologies), they have it enabled. 

Learning patterns for HP impact:

* Because of the point 2 above, we are not at a position where we can learn this. Made a recommendation to have HP set for all the campaigns if HP efficiency is a metric of importance


Also proposed the following change in the way HP is setup (usually a fraction of users who get campaigns are put into HP)

*current setup:*
DP: Treatment proportion: 90%, control proportion: 10%
HP (10% sample from both groups): Treatment proportion: 9%, control proportion: 1%I see that there are very few records in control at a cohort level because of this
*proposed setup*
DP: Treatment proportion: 90%, control proportion: 10%
HP: Treatment proportion: 5%, control proportion: 5%

This might increase the significance for the same opportunity cost (not targeting 10% of the population)
This task is deprioritised until we collect more HP data

CS agents should not be sending outgoing tickets for refunds, as it’s not documented in any CS process. We are aware that Bolt not informing the driver about something that affects their balance is also very problematic here.

This also recently became an issue in the UK market as drivers were complaining, and we raised this with the product teams. Work is in progress (or at least planned for Q4) by the Commerce and Driver App teams to implement the following two solutions:

# Commerce team (more specifically Billing Rides team) will emit an event after a refund so that the lifecycle team can listen to it and build their communication on top of that.
# Driver app team will ensure the refund information is available on the order detail level (ideally tapping the push message should open this screen).

It has been confirmed that our T&Cs allow us to make deductions from the driver’s balance without comms, so it’s fine for CS agents not to send manual outgoing tickets. 

The reason we do not include the step to inform the driver via outgoing message in our KB procedures is that previous research showed that these messages don’t even get opened, yet as you mentioned, there is a cost that CS bears by sending outgoing messages (plus it’s not technically possible in Beehive). 

So… long story short is that a fix is being worked on, and this should not be an action completed by CS.

I honestly do not remember making this joke but I will admit that I can see myself making it, with the sole goal of lightening the mood and diffusing the tension as Amida was anxious about the situation.

According to the Employment, Social Affairs & Inclusion for Estonia 

_Pregnancy and maternity leave will become maternity leave with the amendment of the law on 1_^_st_^ _of April. A woman has the right to maternity leave of 100 calendar days, which becomes collectible at least 70 calendar days before the estimated date of birth. If a woman starts using maternity leave less than 70 days before the estimated date of birth, the maternity leave is shortened by the respective period. This means that the length of maternity leave will depend on when the mother goes on maternity leave._

The amendment of the law took place on 1st of April 2022, there is only 100 days of maternity leave available in Estonia.

After you have applied for the Maternity Leave through the self-service of the[ Social Insurance Board|https://iseteenindus.sotsiaalkindlustusamet.ee/dashboard/portal/login?url=%2Fdashboard%2Fportal] (add [+peopleops@bolt.eu+|mailto:peopleops@bolt.eu] and [+payroll.ee@bolt.eu+|mailto:payroll.ee@bolt.eu]) raise a [People Service Desk|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/6] ticket or contact your People Partner to add the leave to Workday.

Also, we as a company should not accept leaving big chunks of GMV behind because of bureaucratic requirements. unless major risks are involved. In that sense: i. what is the risk for Bolt in sharing such documents with high standards banks such as CRDB or ABSA? ii. how can a letter from their side change the amount of risk we are taking?  iii. could we create a standard procedure to identify companies we are not willing to share the docs at any cost from those we can share docs? We had the meeting on Monday with Francisco Pita (CCO) and Pedro Leitao (Parking Manager)

We discussed different proposals for the pick-up and drop-off for TDVE & taxis and the legal arguments that underpin them. 

They are aligned with the legal arguments but ANA's legal team considers that there is still a grey area. Although they know the right granted in the concession contract (and their position back in 2015), they are some doubts around this: (1) whether or not taxis can be moved to another area and (2) TDVE can use the terminal curbside, in arrivals (pick-up) and departures (drop-off). 

Your opinion on this and the feedback from the City Council will be very important. We told ANA that DLA made the consultation and ANA will include it in their analysis. 

To clarify a little bit, we proposed to:

* Use the arrival terminal curbise as TDVE pick-up point and relocate taxis elsewhere (near the terminal). Since ANA doesn't want to argue with taxis, we proposed to share the terminal curbside because there is an area that is not used (see below).  
* Use the departure terminal curbside as drop-off point with taxis (shared)

We proposed to do a pilot (low season at the airport) but they argued that TDVE cannot use this area. 

They are currently discussing with their legal and technical team several options to relocate TDVE to an area that is not the best for us, hence the outcome of the consultation will be necessary as soon as possible to have the opportunity to build a strong proposal.

Update from DLA, 4 Nov:



We have insisted a few more times and have met the same wall of the silence, and have therefore given up on extracting from them in a collaborative manner. We have *launched a judicial intimation at the administrative court on 28 October and the City Council were served just yesterday*. They have now 10 days to respond to the court, subject to committing a disobedience felony. Our experience in similar cases is that public entities avoid by all means being convicted for failure to act once they are served with an intimation such as the one the City Council was served with yesterday.

In our opinion, this should not be a cause for you to lose momentum with ANA. As we see it, you are in a position to proceed your negotiation with ANA based on the following assumptions:

# The City Council has refused to respond to the consultation and thus, there is nothing contradicting the view sustaining that it is ANA, and not the City Council, having the power to decide on pick-up and drop-oof points at the airport concession area. Our opinion is that the City Council has refused to respond in order to avoid having to acknowledge that the poeer belongs to ANA. No matter what they say now (if at all), their silence so far in spite of the many insistences on our part allows for this interpretation;
# The assessment made by the Portuguese Competition Authority is clear and the finding of dominance by ANA places them under a legal obligation to avoid discrimination and subject them to heavy penalties under competition rules if they failo to act to avoid any such discrimination.

We’ll naturally follow-up any development in the context of the pending court proceedings and will keep you posted. But we believe that the two assumptions described above provide you with a sufficiently solid basis to push your agenda with ANA and avoid losing momentum.

required metrics


{code:sql}
with orders AS (
	SELECT
	                company_order__city_id as city_id,
	                company_order__id AS order_id,
		company_order__user_id AS user_id,
		company_order__state AS o_state,
		company_order__created o_created,
		company_order_try__id as ot_id,
		company_order_try__state AS ot_state,
		company_order_try__created ot_created,
	    datediff('seconds',company_order__created,min_order_try ) as order_to_first_order_try_diff,
        count_order_try

	FROM etl_search_denormalized_view v
	left join (select ott.order_id as o_id, ott.city_id as c_id, min(created) as min_order_try, count(created) as count_order_try
	    from company_order_try ott
	    group by 1,2
	    ) ottt on ottt.o_id=v.company_order__id and ottt.c_id=v.company_order__city_id

	WHERE company_order_try__retry_to_try is null
		AND not nvl(duplicate_order, false)
       ----and city_id in (437,271,137,54)
)
,
orders_agg AS (
	SELECT
		o.user_id,
        test_id,
	    treatment_name,
        city_ID,
		count( distinct o.order_id) as order_count,
	    avg(order_to_first_order_try_diff) as order_to_first_order_try_diff,
	    avg(order_to_last_order_try_diff) as order_to_last_order_try_diff,
        sum(count_order_try) as count_order_try,
        avg(count_order_try) as avg_order_try,
        sum(case when ot_id is not null then 1 else 0 end ) as matched_order_count,
		sum(case when ot_state = 'finished' then 1 else 0 end ) as finished_order_count,
	    sum(case when o_state = 'cancelled' then 1 else 0 end ) as cancelled_order_count,
        sum(case when o_state = 'no_driver_provided' then 1 else 0 end ) as no_driver_provided_order_count


	FROM orders o
	group by 1,2,3,4
),

	select
	u.user_id,
    order_to_first_order_try_diff as time_until_first_match,
    coalesce(avg_order_try,0) as avg_order_try,
    case when coalesce(o.order_count,0) = 0 then 0 else coalesce(o.matched_order_count,0)*1.0000/coalesce(o.order_count,0)*1.0000 end as matched_order_rate,
    case when coalesce(o.order_count,0) = 0 then 0 else coalesce(o.no_driver_provided_order_count,0)*1.0000/coalesce(o.order_count,0)*1.0000 end as no_driver_provided_order_rate,
    coalesce(o.no_driver_provided_order_count,0) no_driver_provided_order_count

	from users u
    left join orders_agg o on o.user_id = u.user_id and o.test_id=u.test_id and o.treatment_name=u.treatment_name and s.city_id=o.city_id{code}
